prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The five views show a shop interior with long shelving/counters across the lower foreground and middle distance, a back wall ahead, and a corridor or doorway toward the right; the ceiling remains above and appears nearest in the map along with foreground fixtures. In frame 1, a person is partly cut off at the far left roughly 1–2 m away, while the shelving extends from about 1 m to several metres away; in frames 2–3, a person near the central counter is approximately 2–4 m away, and farther figures near the right corridor are roughly 4–7 m away. Across frames 3–5, the counter and nearby person shift left in the image as the camera wearer turns or moves right, while the corridor and distant people become more frontal; relative person-to-person separations appear to be roughly 2–5 m. The depth map makes the foreground-versus-background layering, ceiling proximity, doorway recess, and partial occlusions by counters clearer than RGB alone, but it has smeared object boundaries, inconsistent brightness near lights and ceiling, and insufficient accuracy for precise metre estimates or gaze direction.
descriptions.segmentation: The map isolates people in each view and a bottle in frame 1: one person is clipped by the left edge about 1–2 m from the camera wearer, the bottle lies to that person’s right and farther back near the shelving, and later people stand behind or beside the counter roughly 2–5 m away. Frames 2–3 contain a prominent person near the middle-left or centre, while frames 4–5 show two separated people around the counter/corridor region, one left of the other by roughly 1–3 m; some additional RGB-visible shelves, counters, and distant figures are not segmented. The masks clarify which visible fragments belong to separate people and reveal partial occlusion by the counter, but they do not directly encode depth, front-versus-back ordering, facing direction, gaze, or arm’s reach, so those can only be estimated from RGB and mask position. The map looks unreliable where labels are truncated, masks cover only small body fragments, one frame assigns two colours to overlapping person regions, and most objects and body parts are omitted.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is empty in frames 1, 2, 4, and 5 and shows only a short magenta hand trajectory in frame 3, located above the lower scene fixtures and slightly left of that frame’s centre. Relative to the RGB frame, this hand is roughly 1–2 m from the camera wearer and within the wearer’s likely arm’s reach, extending diagonally down and right; no yellow body skeleton is detected, so the hand cannot be assigned a reliable body orientation or gaze direction. The hand points lie close together and show the hand’s local shape or motion more distinctly than RGB, but they provide no dependable locations for the other people, no person-to-person distances, and no evidence of approach or retreat across the five frames. The map is highly incomplete and therefore unreliable for whole-body pose, occlusions, facing direction, or temporal movement beyond the single detected hand trace.
